backlog.hypothesis: CONCLUDED 2026-06-15 (keep). Same-channel 🔍 REVIEW prefix on status∈{NO_ANIMAL,UNCLASSIFIABLE} flags 99% of FP at 0 FN; live since 06-12, location-agnostic. Second-channel routing is OUT per Daniel (no 2nd channel — adds overhead, won't click two). See runs/0001 + LEARNINGS.
Raise SPECIES_UNKNOWN_SPECIES_THRESHOLD 0.5 -> 0.75. Replay-gated; parked until replay.py is real.

CONCLUDED 2026-06-17 (not viable in current scene). In-tick spatial diagnostic (diff burst frames → motion centroid, 70 labeled detections w/ frames on disk: 18 real-animal incl wrong_species, 52 FP). FP and animal motion centroids are spatially ENTANGLED — both center-weighted (median ~0.5/0.5). NO edge band removes FP without removing a comparable-or-greater share of animals: left15% catches 8%FP vs 17%animals (hurts animals MORE), right15% 12%FP vs 11%animals (wash), top15% 10%FP vs 11%animals (wash), bottom15% 0 animals but only 1/52 FP (negligible). No zero-observed-FN ROI exists → FN-veto stands on data, not assumption. Reinforces exp #4 (motion knobs don't separate FP from animal) + exp #1 (notification-layer REVIEW prefix is the right architecture, not trigger-side suppression). See JOURNAL 2026-06-17.

USER-FLAGGED (Daniel, 2026-06-09): many FP are recurrent near-identical static scenes that MOG2 background subtraction should have absorbed. Diagnose why repeated/static frames aren't suppressed (central-region weighting re-amplifying same edge motion, motion_threshold 500px too low vs MOG2 residual noise, learning rate / history=500 vs trigger cadence, shadow/lighting drift) before tuning. Potentially high-impact FP reduction. See JOURNAL 2026-06-09 user note.

CONCLUDED 2026-07-07 (shipped). Daniel's product/privacy call: SUPPRESS human alerts entirely (no Telegram, not REVIEW-tagged); saved photos of HUMAN-status detections kept 48h then purged, DB row kept as metadata-only. Fix shipped as a MegaDetector person-gate (human_detection_confidence>=0.3) OR homo-taxon check, evaluated before the animal branch — broader than the originally-proposed taxon-only REVIEW-tag fix, since most human captures are blurry NO_ANIMAL/UNCLASSIFIABLE frames never tagged 'homo'. New config: SPECIES_HUMAN_DETECTION_CONFIDENCE, PERFORMANCE_SUPPRESS_HUMAN_ALERTS, PERFORMANCE_HUMAN_RETENTION_HOURS; new DetectionStatus.HUMAN. Shipped on branch fix/human-gate-blur-gate. Leak-watch continues post-deploy as verification. See runs/0004 Resolution + JOURNAL 2026-07-08.

CONCLUDED 2026-07-07 (shipped). The sharpness floor (min_sharpness_threshold=11.0) in _capture_and_select_best_frame silently discarded low-light/dusk captures (return None,None before DB logging or notification), causing unrecorded false negatives — e.g. the 07-07 ~19:10 pond bird detected 17x across 4 captured bursts, never logged. Fix: below-floor bursts now always get species ID + a DB row; alert if an animal is found (even blurry), mute (DB-log only, no Telegram) if not, so REVIEW volume does not rise. fn_risk down, fp_rate unchanged. Shipped on branch fix/human-gate-blur-gate. See runs/0005 + JOURNAL 2026-07-08.

ROLLED BACK 2026-07-09 (same day as ship). AE=short was meant to raise dusk sharpness_score above the 11.0 floor. Measurement on saved frames shows it CANNOT: sharpness_score is Laplacian variance, which scales with frame contrast/brightness; AE=short lowers luma by construction (19h matched-hour: luma 68.9->52.0), so it pushes MORE bursts below the floor, not fewer. Run 0006's own pre-registered 'midday regression => reconsider' trigger also fired (16h lap 19.18->15.07). FN unmeasured + plausible FN rise via the below-floor+no-animal mute path => FN-veto => reverted to AE=normal. Reopened as running to collect the matched-hour 17-19h AE=normal baseline that was never captured. CONCLUDED 2026-07-10: AE=normal dusk baseline now in (07-10 17-18h sharpness 6.9-9.4) and is indistinguishable from AE=short (07-09 17-18h 7.8-8.6) — both below the 11.0 floor. AE mode is not the lever; the floor statistic is (backlog id 8, now active). AE=normal retained. See runs/0006.

ROOT CAUSE behind exp #6/#5. min_sharpness_threshold=11.0 is applied to raw Laplacian variance, a whole-frame contrast statistic, so it functions as a SCENE-BRIGHTNESS gate, not a blur gate. Measured on 470 pre-deploy frames (AE=normal, multi-day): P(lap<11.0) = 0% for luma>=80, 71% for luma 60-80, 100% for luma<40. Consequence: at dusk nearly every burst is 'below floor' regardless of actual motion blur, so the blur-gate mute path (below-floor AND no animal found -> no Telegram) is reachable mainly as a function of light level. Fix candidates: (a) brightness- normalized sharpness (lap/gray_var) as the floor statistic, (b) make the floor luma-dependent, (c) drop the mute path and rely on the REVIEW prefix. Needs a code change, not an env knob.

PROPOSED 2026-07-13 (exp #5 leak-watch first hit). The human/privacy gate leaked a person's photo to the MAIN channel: id 1988 (07-13 19:50) status=identified, ensemble species_name generic ';;;;;;animal' (conf 0.72 -> notifies, Best-guess line would read 'human 59%'), because (1) MegaDetector person box 0.10 < human_detection_confidence 0.30, and (2) the ensemble rolled the classifier's homo-sapiens top-1 up to a generic 'animal' label with no 'homo' taxon segment, so both existing gate paths missed it. Fix: also fire DetectionStatus.HUMAN when the RAW classifier top-1 (top_species_raw / metadata['top_classifier_prediction']) contains a 'homo' taxon AND the ensemble did not confidently ID a specific animal (generic/blank/no-cv/review-class), so a confident species ID is never overridden. Specificity across the WHOLE DB: top_species_raw~homo occurs on exactly 2 rows (1852, 1988), both actual humans, 0 real animals -> catches both with 0 observed false-suppression; FN risk negligible on evidence. Code change (no env knob reaches it); subagent-driven TDD, commit separately w/ exp id, restart-gated. HELD for Daniel's explicit OK because it modifies the privacy-suppression gate (his strongest product lever) and FN is formally unmeasured. See runs/0007 'CROSS-CUTTING FINDING' 2026-07-13.

nightly_verdict: Heads up: one photo of a person slipped past the privacy filter tonight (about 7:50pm, during a family-in-the-garden evening) and reached your normal alerts labelled 'human' - the filter hid the other 22 correctly, but this one got through because the person was blurry and close and the AI's main guess came out vague. I've found the exact cause and a targeted fix that would have caught it (plus a similar near-miss yesterday) with no risk to real animal alerts, but since it changes the privacy filter I'm holding it for your OK before switching it on. No real animals were missed; and the camera is still noticeably out of focus, so a quick focus check is worth doing when you can.
